newsitem.title: BULGARIA: BULGARIA FINANCE MINISTRY CLAIMS $40 MLN FROM FPB.
newsitem.headline: BULGARIA FINANCE MINISTRY CLAIMS $40 MLN FROM FPB.

text.p: Bulgaria's finance ministry has filed a claim against First Private Bank (FPB) asking it to repay $40 million and seven billion levs spent on compensation for deposits, Finance Minister Dimitar Kostov said on Thursday.
On Wednesday, the Sofia city court rejected an insolvency suit against FPB by the central bank, which put FPB in receivership in May.
"If the court says the bank is solvent it should be able to meet its payments and we have claimed the compensation payments on its deposits," Kostov told a news conference.

FPB's sequestrators, appointed in May by the central bank to establish its financial situation, said the bank's state had improved as it had collected some loans but it would not repay the deposit compensations because the central bank decision was unjustified.
Under a deposit guarantee law passed earlier this year, when a bank is declared bankrupt individual savers are compensated in full while firms can retrieve up to half of their savings.
Deposits in bankrupt banks are serviced by the State Savings Bank and the state-owned Bulgarian Post Bank.

The BNB placed 14 or one quarter of Bulgaria's banks in receivership and has so far filed insolvency suits against nine banks in line with pledges made to the International Monetary Fund to close debt-ridden banks to stabilise the banking sector.

Under the law, the government issued treasury bonds worth a total of 80 billion levs and $100 million, which were placed with the State Savings Bank and the Bulgarian Post Bank to guarantee payments to depositors in the first five banks placed in receivership.
The law was amended later so that deposits are compensated only after the court declares the banks bankrupt.
